transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Morgan (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Sana Iqbal (notes), Rajesh Patel (CTO - Clarion), Marta Alvarez (Lead ML), Tom Burns (PM), Lina Chen (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync for the ongoing quantization POC. Focus on unexpected quality variance observed across prompt families after INT8 conversion, compare to FP8 runs, and agree next steps for triage and perf benchmarks on dedicated capacity. Key asks: reproducible regression list, tokenizer edge cases, and dedicated perf runs with warm/cold KV cache.

Topics covered:
- High-level: which prompts regressed and by how much (qual + metric deltas)
- Repro steps: seeds, tokenizer versions, decode strategy (sampling vs beam)
- Perf: tokens/sec, latency p50/p95/p99 on INT8 vs FP8, batching behaviour
- Ops: KV cache warm/cold effects, fallback policies, Dedicated vs Hosted routing
- Security/compliance touchpoints: KMS, SOC2, VPC network restriction notes

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia (Redwood): Okay team, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes-ish, demo and triage, then next steps. Rajesh, you want to kick off with the top-level pain?
[00:12] Rajesh (Clarion): Yeah thanks, so overall the pilot looked great on throughput, we saw about 2.8x tokens per second improvement with INT8 on your shared env, but Marta's team flagged a cluster of prompts where the extracts are lower quality, like missing entities and sometimes hallucinating new medication names, which is -- I mean it's a big no for us.
[00:30] Marta (Clarion): Yup, and it's not all prompts. It's specific families — multi-hop extraction + long context summarization. Metrics: ROUGE-L drop of 4-6 pts for some buckets, F1 entity match down 8-12%. 
[00:46] Devon (Redwood SE): Got it. Thanks for the detail. A couple quick clarifying Qs — are you using the same sampling/temperature and are you seeding the runs? Also which tokenizer version is in your pipeline?
[00:58] Marta: We're seeding for the evals but not every production run. We used BPE-v2 tokenizer v1.3 — that is the same as the baseline run. Temperature 0.0 for extractive tasks, 0.7 for summarization.
[01:12] Alicia: Okay perfect. When you say FP8 vs INT8, did you run FP8 with the same kernels and also the fallback profile?
[01:20] Rajesh: We ran FP8 on the dedicated subset last week with reduced batch sizes, but not the exact same fallback profile, I think. Lina can confirm.
[01:28] Lina: Confirming, FP8 run had a smaller batch config and we didn't enable per-token fallback. That could be a difference.
[01:36] Devon: That helps. What we're hearing is variance concentrated in longer-context multi-hop prompts and some tokenizer edge cases. Two hypotheses: (1) quantization noise amplifies on long KV cache chains, (2) per-channel quant vs per-tensor scaling leads to certain attention weight distortion on small-value heads. Both could cause entity drop.
[01:55] Tom (PM): We also saw some non-deterministic differences between runs on the same model/config. Is that expected with INT8?
[02:03] Devon: Some nondet can happen depending on rounding and accumulation ordering on GPU kernels, especially with mixed precision paths. INT8 can be more sensitive to ordering of ops and fused kernels. We should be able to make runs deterministic for eval by fixing RNG seeds and forcing deterministic cuDNN settings — we'll include that in repro steps.
[02:20] Marta: Good. For triage, we need a reproducible list of top 50 failure prompts and the per-token logprob traces if possible.
[02:28] Alicia: We can do that. We'll generate per-token logprobs for the flagged prompts. Devon, do you want to speak to the perf delta numbers we saw?
[02:36] Devon: Sure. On the hosted baseline we measured ~420 tokens/sec p50 for FP16, with INT8 on the shared pilot we got about 1,150 tps p50. FP8 ran about 1,000 tps but with slightly higher variance when batching. On dedicated GPUs with KV cache warm, INT8 can hit 1,350 tps depending on batch packing. p95 latency was still acceptable but p99 for long contexts got closer to SLOs. Those numbers are preliminary — we'll run a dedicated cluster benchmark to produce the CSV.
[03:04] Rajesh: That's promising on perf but we need the quality fix first. If INT8 can't meet entity extraction thresholds, we might need to use FP8 or selective layer fallback.
[03:14] Devon: Fully agree. We have a couple tactical approaches: 1) selective fallback (keep first N layers in FP16 or FP8), 2) per-channel quantization for linear layers that affect attention, 3) bias folding disabled for sensitive heads — though that can increase model size. We can test those in parallel.
[03:33] Marta: Can you explain bias folding? We saw that term in the notes but want concrete impact.
[03:38] Devon: Sure — bias folding moves bias into adjacent weights to reduce quantization error overall. For some small heads, folding can amplify small weight values and the quant scale becomes coarser, so sensitive attention scores shift. Disabling folding for a subset can keep those heads closer to baseline. It's a tradeoff with model size and perf.
[03:55] Alicia: Also a reminder that tokenization mismatches can look like model regressions. Lina, you mentioned tokenizer edge cases?
[04:02] Lina: Right — around punctuation and hybrid tokens like drug names that mix caps and hyphens we saw token offsets change after quantized decoding. We'll extract the top 20 problematic prompts where token boundaries differ between baseline and quantized outputs.
[04:16] Rajesh: Can Redwood share a suggested eval harness? We'll run it in our CI nightly.
[04:21] Alicia: Yes, we'll share a harness — includes fixed seeds, exact tokenizer binaries, decode params, and the per-token logprob capture. We'll also include a small script to diff token offsets.
[04:33] Marta: Great. On the perf side, curious about KV cache warm vs cold effect magnitude you mentioned; do you have numbers?
[04:40] Devon: Anecdotally, cold cache adds about 10-25% latency for long contexts since we can't reuse prefix states; warm cache gives steady-state throughput. We'll instrument with both warm/cold runs and surface p50/p95/p99. Also we'll capture memory pressure and any out-of-memory fallback events.
[04:58] Tom: From procurement / ops perspective, if we move to Dedicated, what's the expected SLA and the sizing? Also curious cost delta between INT8 and FP8 profiles.
[05:08] Alicia: Dedicated provides SLA-backed capacity. Cost depends on committed tiers; INT8 gives best cost-per-token but FP8 often sits between INT8 and FP16 in price. We'll include a simple cost model in the pricing sheet we send — tokens/sec and expected tokens per session map to monthly spend.
[05:21] Rajesh: Also security — we need to ensure KMS integration and that logs of user data are not persisted in your control plane. Where are we on that?
[05:29] Alicia: We will share SOC 2 artifacts and our KMS integration doc. For Private deployments we can provide a customer-controlled control plane and HSM/KMS options. For Hosted pilots, we can redact PII and configure retention windows. We'll attach the security package.
[05:44] Marta: Back to triage, could we run an experiment: pick 3 mitigation configs — per-channel quant, disable bias fold on top-6 heads, and selective FP8-first-2-layers — and compare quality metrics across the top 500 prompts?
[05:57] Devon: Yes, we can bake those as separate variants and run the 500-prompt set in parallel; it'll require compute but doable on dedicated cluster. Expect results in ~48 hours once we have the exact prompt set.
[06:08] Alicia: So to confirm next steps: Clarion to push the 500-1k prompt suite and flags to us; Redwood will run the three mitigation variants plus baseline INT8 and FP8 and return: per-prompt deltas, per-token logprobs for failures, and perf CSVs (warm/cold KV cache).
[06:25] Rajesh: Correct. Also please annotate examples where tokenization caused the problem vs true hallucination.
[06:32] Lina: We'll export tokenizer binary and a sample trace.
[06:36] Marta: One more question — how do we handle routing/fallback in production? If a request fails the quality check, can you route to FP8 or to a higher-tier model automatically?
[06:45] Devon: Yes, we support policy-based routing. You can define a confidence threshold or an eval hook that marks output as low-quality, then route to a fallback model (FP8 or FP16) or to a canary. There's a config snippet we'll share. Note that routing to a fallback increases latency for those sessions.
[06:59] Tom: That sounds workable. For dashboards, can you show token-level cost breakdown so we can estimate spend by prompt family?
[07:06] Alicia: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route token breakdown and token-type cost. We'll enable a temporary dashboard for your account for the pilot.
[07:13] Rajesh: Any quick wins you recommend while we wait for the big runs?
[07:17] Devon: A couple: 1) dereive a short list of top 50 failing prompts and run with deterministic seeds to see if the error is consistent; 2) try per-layer scaling adjustments for the top 2 layers in head groups; 3) confirm tokenizer binaries match and use exact decode options.
[07:30] Marta: We'll get the prompt exports today.
[07:33] Alicia: Great. We'll target sharing the benchmark outputs by Monday 12/1. We'll also send the security docs and suggested config JSON by Thursday 11/28.
[07:42] Rajesh: Sounds good. Anything else?
[07:44] Lina: Small note — Clarion's infra team will need an IP allowlist for the dedicated run, will send contacts to Alicia.
[07:51] Alicia: Noted. Please send the contact and we'll coordinate.
[07:54] Sana (notes): capturing action items and next steps in the notes channel.
[08:00] Alicia: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene 12/4 for triage with results.

End recap (as recorded):
- Primary issue: quality regressions on INT8 concentrated in multi-hop extraction and long-context summarization (ROUGE/F1 drops).
- Hypotheses: tokenizer edge cases, accumulation/rounding noise in INT8 kernels, bias folding and per-tensor quant scaling causing small-head distortion.
- Tactical mitigations to test: per-channel quant, selective disable bias folding, selective FP8/FP16 layers, deterministic runs.
- Deliverables: 1) Redwood: perf CSVs (warm/cold), per-prompt delta lists, config snips; 2) Clarion: prompt suite + tokenizer binary + contact for IP allowlist.
